newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government delays crop forecast on floods.
newsitem.headline: Thai government delays crop forecast on floods.

text.p: Thailand's agriculture ministry has postponed the 1996/97 crop forecast for rice, corn, soybean and sugar cane due to floods, a ministry official said on Tuesday.
The figures were originally due to be released in the last week of September. But officials said they have to revise the figures to reflect the current situation.
"We have to redo the whole forecast to factor in the latest flood damage. The complete forecast should be available later this week," the offcial told Reuters.

The ministry revises crop data every second month. The previous forecast put the first crop rice output for 1996/97 (April-March) at 18.11 million tonnes, corn (July-June) at 4.36 million tonnes, soybean (April-March) at 411,916 tonnes and sugar cane (Nov-Oct) at 62.42 million tonnes.
According to the latest Interior Ministry figure, floods have damaged 556,919 hectares (1.4 million acres) of farmland, of which 397,859 hectares (995,000 acres) were rice fields.
